def palindromic_suffix_array_count(s, k):
    """Count palindromes sharing the suffix array of s.

    The suffix array of a string t of length n is the permutation
    sa[0..n-1] of {0, ..., n-1} such that the suffixes
    t[sa[0]:], t[sa[1]:], ..., t[sa[n-1]:] are in strictly increasing
    lexicographic order.  (All suffixes of one string are pairwise
    distinct, so the suffix array is unique -- no tie-breaking needed.)

    Given a string s (1 <= len(s) <= 200, lowercase letters 'a'-'z')
    and an integer k (1 <= k <= 26), return the exact number of strings
    t such that:
      * len(t) == len(s),
      * every character of t is one of the first k lowercase letters,
      * t is a palindrome (t == t[::-1]), and
      * t has exactly the same suffix array as s.

    The result is an exact Python int (it may be large; no modulus is
    applied).  Return 0 when no such t exists.  s itself need not be a
    palindrome, and t is not required to use the same letters as s.
    If len(s) == 1 the suffix array is always [0] and every single
    letter is a palindrome, so the answer is k.

    >>> palindromic_suffix_array_count("aa", 2)
    2
    >>> palindromic_suffix_array_count("abacaba", 4)
    4
    >>> palindromic_suffix_array_count("ab", 26)
    0
    """
